objects.definition: typedef signed short       int16;
objects.description: Alias for signed 16-bit integer type.

objects.definition: typedef signed int         int32;
objects.description: Alias for signed 32-bit integer type.

objects.definition: typedef signed long long   int64;
objects.description: Alias for signed 64-bit integer type.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned char      uint8;
objects.description: Alias for unsigned 8-bit integer type.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned short     uint16;
objects.description: Alias for unsigned 16-bit integer type.

objects.description: Alias for unsigned 32-bit integer type.

objects.description: Alias for unsigned 64-bit integer type.
2D vector of floats with common arithmetic, dot/cross, normalization, rotation and lerp utilities.
3D vector of floats with arithmetic, dot/cross products, normalization, rotations, and helper accessors to sub-vectors.
4D vector/point with arithmetic and dot product, access to sub-vectors, and lerp.
Quaternion for rotations with operations, vector rotation, normalization, inverse, and lerp/slerp.
4x4 column-major matrix with projection building, transforms, inversion, transpose, composition, and element-wise interpolation. Includes ProjRange enum inside.
Rigid transform basis combining rotation (quat) and translation (vec3). Supports composition, inverse, and interpolation.
Two unsigned bytes container, typically for compact 2D data/indices.
4-component unsigned byte vector packed in a union with a 32-bit value.
Pair of 16-bit signed integers with equality operator.
Triple of 16-bit signed integers with basic arithmetic and cast to vec3.
Four 16-bit signed integers with conversions to smaller short vectors and float vectors.
Sphere with center and radius; supports sphere-sphere and ray-sphere intersection tests.
Axis-aligned bounding box with many operations: union/intersection, transforms, ray and sphere intersections, translation and rotations by 90 degrees.
32-bit RGBA color union with helpers to set from RGB555 and convert YCbCr 4:2:0 blocks to four RGBA pixels.
24-bit RGB color struct with implicit conversion to Color32.
16-bit RGBA (5-5-5-1) color union with conversions to 24-bit and 32-bit formats.
16-bit RGBA (5-5-5-1) color union intended for color lookup tables with conversions to RGB24/RGBA32.
Two 4-bit indices packed into a single byte, for 4bpp tiles.
4-bit indexed tile image data for 256x256 texture (two pixels per byte).
8-bit indexed tile image data for 256x256 texture.
16-bit color tile image data for 256x256 texture.
Texture atlas color type. It is either a 16-bit RGBA5551 union (when USE_ATLAS_RGBA16 is defined) or an alias of Color32 otherwise. Note: actual compiled form depends on build flags.
Tile structure holding 256x256 atlas texels of type AtlasColor.
32-bit RGBA tile image data for 256x256 texture.
Color Look-Up Table of 16 RGBA5551 entries.

I/O stream abstraction supporting file and memory-backed reads, caching/buffering, pack (ZIP central directory) lookup, and static helpers for cache operations. Includes nested types Pack and Pack::FileInfo.
direct_api_constructors: Stream(const char *name, const void *data, int size, Callback *callback = NULL, void *userData = NULL)
Stream(const char *name, Callback *callback = NULL, void *userData = NULL)

objects.description: Nested helper within Stream that represents a ZIP pack file with a parsed central directory table and search for uncompressed entries.
Small POD inside Stream::Pack holding file size and offset to local header/payload inside the pack.
Utility for reading variable-width bit fields from a byte stream with both little-endian and big-endian bit ordering helpers.
Fixed-size character array wrapper template with copy/assign helper; str16 is an alias for 16-char buffer.

functions.name: sincos
functions.description: Computes both sine and cosine of angle r (radians) and stores the results in *s and *c. On PSP builds, this maps to vfpu_sincos; otherwise it calls sinf and cosf.
requirements: s and c must be valid, non-null pointers to float locations for output.
r is an angle in radians.

functions.name: min
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline const T& min(const T &a, const T &b)
functions.description: Returns the smaller of a and b by strict operator< comparison.
requirements: T must support operator< and be copyable/addressable.
Arguments must remain valid as the returned reference may alias an argument.

functions.name: max
functions.signature: template <class T> inline const T& max(const T &a, const T &b)
functions.description: Returns the larger of a and b by strict operator> comparison.
requirements: T must support operator>.
Returned reference aliases one of the inputs; they must remain valid.

functions.name: clamp
functions.signature: template <class T> inline const T clamp(const T &x, const T &a, const T &b)
functions.description: Clamps x to the inclusive range [a, b]. Returns a if x<a, b if x>b, otherwise x.
requirements: T must support operator< and operator> comparisons.

functions.name: sign
functions.signature: template <class T> inline const T sign(const T &x)
functions.description: Returns 1 if x>0, -1 if x<0, otherwise 0, converted to T.
requirements: T must be constructible from integer literals -1, 0, 1, and support comparisons with 0.

functions.name: swap
functions.signature: template <class T> inline void swap(T &a, T &b)
functions.description: Swaps the values of a and b using a temporary.
requirements: a and b must be valid references to the same type T.

functions.name: swap16
functions.description: Byte-swaps a 16-bit unsigned integer (endianness swap).

functions.name: swap32
functions.description: Byte-swaps a 32-bit unsigned integer (endianness swap).

functions.name: clampAngle
functions.description: Wraps angle a (radians) into the range (-PI, PI].
requirements: Input is interpreted in radians.

functions.name: shortAngle
functions.description: Computes the shortest signed angular difference from a to b (radians), wrapped to (-PI, PI].
requirements: Inputs are interpreted in radians.

functions.name: normalizeAngle
functions.description: Normalizes angle to [0, 2*PI]. Values below 0 are increased by 2*PI until in-range; above 2*PI are decreased accordingly.
requirements: Input angle is in radians.

functions.name: angleQuadrant
functions.description: Returns the quadrant index (0..3) for angle+PI*offset after normalization to [0, 2*PI], using 90-degree sectors.
requirements: Angles are radians.
offset is scaled by PI before applying.

functions.name: decrease
functions.description: Adjusts value towards its target by moving it by speed in the direction of delta, clamped not to overshoot. Returns the applied delta (new speed) or 0 if no movement.
requirements: Function assumes speed>0 and |delta|>0.001f to change value; otherwise returns 0.
value and speed are modified in place.

functions.name: hermite
functions.description: Cubic Hermite smoothstep function 3x^2 - 2x^3, typically used for smooth interpolation when x in [0,1].
requirements: For canonical smoothstep behavior, pass x within [0,1].

functions.name: quintic
functions.description: Quintic smoothstep function x^3(6x^2 - 15x + 10), for smoother interpolation with zero first and second derivatives at endpoints.
requirements: For intended behavior, pass x within [0,1].

functions.name: lerp
functions.signature: inline float lerp(float a, float b, float t)
functions.description: Linear interpolation between a and b by t in [0,1]. Returns a if t<=0, b if t>=1.
requirements: t is typically in [0,1]; outside this range it clamps by early returns.

functions.name: lerpAngle
functions.signature: float lerpAngle(float a, float b, float t)
functions.description: Interpolates from angle a to b along the shortest arc using t in [0,1]. Returns a if t<=0, b if t>=1.
requirements: Angles are radians.
t typically in [0,1].

functions.name: nextPow2
functions.description: Returns the next power-of-two greater than or equal to x. For x==0 the function returns 0 due to underflow during decrement; otherwise returns a power of two.
requirements: Behavior for x==0 returns 0 (note: not a power of two).

functions.name: log2i
functions.description: Returns floor(log2(value)) for value>0; returns 0 when value==0.
requirements: For value==0, result is 0 by definition in this implementation.

functions.name: fnv32
functions.signature: uint32 fnv32(const char *data, int32 size, uint32 hash = 0x811c9dc5)
functions.description: Computes 32-bit FNV-1 hash over size bytes at data, starting from provided initial hash (default offset basis).
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes.
size must be non-negative.

functions.name: qsort
functions.signature: template <class T> void qsort(T* v, int L, int R)
functions.description: In-place quicksort over v[L..R] using static int T::cmp(const T&, const T&) comparator. Partitions and recursively sorts.
requirements: v must be a valid array with indices in [L,R].
L and R must be valid indices, L<=R for non-empty range.
T must provide static int cmp(const T&, const T&), returning <0,0,>0 ordering.
Elements must be swappable with swap(T&,T&).

functions.name: sort
functions.signature: template <class T> void sort(T *items, int count)
functions.description: Sorts an array of count items using the above qsort with a T::cmp comparator.
requirements: items must point to at least count elements when count>0.
T must provide static int cmp(const T&, const T&).

functions.name: Noise::index
functions.signature: uint8 Noise::index(int x, int y, int z)
functions.description: Returns a permutation table index in [0,11] used for gradient lookup, based on 3D integer lattice coordinates.
requirements: Noise::setSeed must be called to initialize tables before use.

functions.name: Noise::noise
functions.signature: float Noise::noise(int x, int y, int z, float xd, float yd, float zd)
functions.description: Computes the dot product of a hashed gradient at cell (x,y,z) with the displacement vector (xd,yd,zd). Used internally by simplex/perlin-like noise.
requirements: Noise::setSeed must have initialized permutation tables.
xd,yd,zd are typically fractional offsets within the cell.

functions.name: Noise::setSeed
functions.description: Initializes the Noise permutation tables using the given seed and std::rand. Fills m_perm and m_perm12 for gradient selection.
requirements: Must be called before using Noise::value or Noise::generate.

functions.name: Noise::value
functions.signature: float Noise::value(float x, float y, float z, int size)
functions.description: Evaluates 3D noise at normalized coordinates (x,y,z) scaled by period size, using quintic interpolation and gradient dot products.
requirements: size must be >0; used as tiling period and for modulo operations.
Noise::setSeed should have been called if deterministic results are desired.

functions.name: Noise::generate
functions.signature: uint8* Noise::generate(uint32 seed, int size, int octaves, int frequency, float amplitude)
functions.description: Generates a 3D noise volume of size^3 bytes using fractal noise with given octaves, starting frequency and amplitude. Returns a newly allocated uint8 array in [0,255] representing normalized noise.
requirements: size must be >0; allocates size*size*size bytes; caller must delete[] the returned pointer.
octaves>=1 typically.
frequency and amplitude control the first octave; frequency doubles and amplitude halves per octave.
May allocate a temporary float buffer of size^3; sufficient memory must be available.

functions.name: vec2::dot
functions.description: Returns the dot product between this vector and v.

functions.name: vec2::cross
functions.description: Returns the 2D scalar cross product x1*y2 - y1*x2.

functions.name: vec2::length2
functions.description: Returns the squared length of the vector.

functions.name: vec2::length
functions.description: Returns the Euclidean length of the vector.

functions.name: vec2::abs
functions.description: Returns a vector with absolute values of components.

functions.name: vec2::normal
functions.description: Returns the normalized vector (unit length). If length is zero, returns the original vector unmodified.

functions.name: vec2::angle
functions.description: Returns the angle in radians of the vector from the +X axis via atan2(y,x).

functions.name: vec2::rotate
functions.description: Rotates the vector by precomputed cosine/sine components cs=(cos,sin): [x',y'] = [x*c - y*s, x*s + y*c].
requirements: cs.x should be cos(theta) and cs.y should be sin(theta) for some angle.

functions.name: vec2::lerp
functions.signature: vec2 vec2::lerp(const vec2 &v, const float t) const
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between this and v by t in [0,1]. Early clamps return endpoints when t<=0 or t>=1.

functions.name: vec3::xy
functions.description: Returns a reference view to the first two components (x,y) as a vec2.
requirements: Returned reference aliases internal storage; use carefully to avoid lifetime issues.

functions.name: vec3::yz
functions.description: Returns a reference view to the (y,z) components as a vec2.
requirements: Returned reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: vec3::dot
functions.description: Returns the dot product with v.

functions.name: vec3::cross
functions.description: Returns the cross product with v.

functions.name: vec3::length2
functions.description: Returns the squared length.

functions.name: vec3::length
functions.description: Returns the Euclidean length.

functions.name: vec3::abs
functions.description: Returns a vector of absolute component values.

functions.name: vec3::normal
functions.description: Returns the normalized vector; returns original if zero length.

functions.name: vec3::axisXZ
functions.description: Returns the dominant axis in the XZ plane as one of (±1,0,0) or (0,0,±1), based on larger absolute component between x and z.

functions.name: vec3::reflect
functions.description: Reflects this vector about normal n: v - 2*dot(v,n)*n.

functions.name: vec3::lerp
functions.signature: vec3 vec3::lerp(const vec3 &v, const float t) const
functions.description: Linear interpolation between this and v with clamping at endpoints for t<=0 or t>=1.

functions.name: vec3::rotateY
functions.description: Returns this vector rotated about Y axis by angle (radians).
requirements: angle in radians.

functions.name: vec3::angle
functions.description: Returns the cosine of the angle between this and v (dot/(|a||b|)). Note: despite the name, it returns cosine, not the angle itself.
requirements: If either vector has zero length, result may be inf/nan.

functions.name: vec3::angleX
functions.description: Returns angle from +Y axis using atan2(sqrt(x^2+z^2), y).

functions.name: vec3::angleY
functions.description: Returns yaw angle in radians via atan2(z, x).

functions.name: vec4::xy
functions.description: Returns a reference view to (x,y) as vec2.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: vec4::xyz
functions.description: Returns a reference view to (x,y,z) as vec3.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: vec4::dot
functions.description: Returns the 4D dot product with v.

functions.name: vec4::lerp
functions.signature: vec4 vec4::lerp(const vec4 &v, const float t) const
functions.description: Linear interpolation with clamping to endpoints for t<=0 or t>=1.

functions.name: quat::xyz
functions.description: Returns a reference view of the vector part (x,y,z) of the quaternion as vec3.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: quat::dot
functions.description: Returns the quaternion dot product with q.

functions.name: quat::length2
functions.description: Returns the squared length of the quaternion.

functions.name: quat::length
functions.description: Returns the length (norm) of the quaternion.

functions.name: quat::normalize
functions.description: Normalizes this quaternion in place to unit length.
requirements: Quaternion length must be non-zero to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: quat::normal
functions.description: Returns the normalized quaternion without modifying this.
requirements: Quaternion length must be non-zero to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: quat::conjugate
functions.description: Returns the conjugate (-x,-y,-z,w).

functions.name: quat::inverse
functions.description: Returns the quaternion inverse: conjugate divided by squared length.
requirements: Quaternion length must be non-zero to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: quat::lerp
functions.signature: quat quat::lerp(const quat &q, float t) const
functions.description: Linear interpolation between this and q without normalization; takes shortest path by flipping q if dot<0. Clamps to endpoints for t<=0 or t>=1.

functions.name: quat::slerp
functions.signature: quat quat::slerp(const quat &q, float t) const
functions.description: Spherical linear interpolation between this and q; handles antipodal quaternions by flipping. Falls back to linear when quaternions are nearly parallel.
requirements: t in [0,1] for typical use.

functions.name: mat4::right
functions.description: Returns a reference to the matrix right (first column) vector.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: mat4::up
functions.description: Returns a reference to the matrix up (second column) vector.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: mat4::dir
functions.description: Returns a reference to the matrix forward/dir (third column) vector.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: mat4::offset
functions.description: Returns a reference to the matrix translation (fourth column) vector.
requirements: Reference aliases internal storage.

functions.name: mat4::ortho
functions.signature: void mat4::ortho(ProjRange range, float l, float r, float b, float t, float znear, float zfar, bool rotate90 = false)
functions.description: Builds an orthographic projection matrix with configurable depth range convention and optional 90-degree rotation.
requirements: r-l and t-b must be non-zero.
znear-zfar must be non-zero.
range must be one of ProjRange values.

functions.name: mat4::frustum
functions.signature: void mat4::frustum(ProjRange range, float l, float r, float b, float t, float znear, float zfar, bool rotate90 = false)
functions.description: Builds a perspective frustum projection matrix with configurable depth range and optional 90-degree rotation.
requirements: r-l, t-b, and znear-zfar must be non-zero.
znear should be >0 and zfar>znear for typical perspective.

functions.name: mat4::perspective
functions.signature: void mat4::perspective(ProjRange range, float fov, float aspect, float znear, float zfar, float eye = 0.0f, bool rotate90 = false)
functions.description: Builds a perspective projection based on vertical fov (degrees), aspect ratio, near/far planes, optional eye offset (asymmetric frustum) and optional 90-degree rotation.
requirements: fov must be >0.
aspect must be >0.
znear and zfar define positive depth range with zfar!=znear.

functions.name: mat4::viewport
functions.signature: void mat4::viewport(float x, float y, float width, float height, float n, float f)
functions.description: Builds a viewport transform mapping NDC to screen coordinates [x,x+width]x[y,y+height] and depth from n to f.
requirements: width and height should be positive.

functions.name: mat4::identity
functions.description: Sets matrix to identity.

functions.name: mat4::translate
functions.description: Post-multiplies this matrix by a translation transform by offset.

functions.name: mat4::scale
functions.description: Post-multiplies this matrix by a non-uniform scale transform.

functions.name: mat4::rotateX
functions.description: Post-multiplies this matrix by a rotation around X axis by angle (radians).
requirements: angle in radians.

functions.name: mat4::rotateY
functions.description: Post-multiplies this matrix by a rotation around Y axis by angle (radians).
requirements: angle in radians.

functions.name: mat4::rotateZ
functions.description: Post-multiplies this matrix by a rotation around Z axis by angle (radians).
requirements: angle in radians.

functions.name: mat4::rotateYXZ
functions.description: Applies in-place rotations to this matrix in Y, then X, then Z order using provided Euler angles (radians). Optimized to modify columns directly.
requirements: Angles in radians.

functions.name: mat4::lerp
functions.description: Linearly interpolates each element toward m by factor t.

functions.name: mat4::det
functions.description: Computes the 4x4 matrix determinant.

functions.name: mat4::inverse
functions.description: Returns the full matrix inverse using adjugate/determinant method.
requirements: Matrix must be invertible (non-zero determinant) to avoid infinities/NaNs.

functions.name: mat4::inverseOrtho
functions.description: Returns the inverse assuming the matrix is an orthonormal transform with translation (no perspective).
requirements: Assumes upper-left 3x3 is orthonormal and bottom row [0,0,0,1].

functions.name: mat4::transpose
functions.description: Returns the transposed matrix.

functions.name: mat4::getRot
functions.description: Extracts a quaternion rotation from the rotation part of the matrix.
requirements: Assumes the matrix encodes a valid rotation in the upper-left 3x3.

functions.name: mat4::setRot
functions.description: Sets the matrix rotation (upper-left 3x3) from a quaternion, without translation or perspective.

functions.name: mat4::getPos
functions.description: Returns the translation vector from the matrix offset column.

functions.name: mat4::setPos
functions.description: Sets the translation vector into the matrix offset column.

functions.name: mat4::rot90
functions.description: Rotates the matrix 90 degrees in X-Y components by swapping elements and flipping signs of the second row (used likely for screen rotation).

functions.name: mat4::unrot90
functions.description: Reverses the 90-degree rotation performed by rot90 by flipping signs then swapping back.

functions.name: Basis::identity
functions.description: Resets Basis to identity rotation, zero position, and w=1.

functions.name: Basis::inverse
functions.description: Returns the inverse rigid transform: inverse rotation (conjugate) and inverse-transformed negative position.
requirements: Assumes unit quaternion rotation for strict inverse; otherwise it uses conjugate (not normalized).

functions.name: Basis::translate
functions.description: Applies a local translation by v to pos (rotates v by current rot and adds).

functions.name: Basis::rotate
functions.description: Applies an additional rotation by quaternion q (post-multiplies).

functions.name: Basis::lerp
functions.description: Linearly interpolates rotation (quat lerp) and position between this and basis by t, returning a new Basis.
requirements: t typically in [0,1].

functions.name: StrUtils::toLower
functions.description: In-place converts ASCII A-Z letters in str to lowercase. Non-ASCII unchanged.
requirements: str may be NULL; function returns immediately in that case.
str must be writable and null-terminated.

functions.name: StrUtils::copy
functions.description: Allocates and returns a heap-allocated copy of the C-string str. Returns NULL if input is NULL.
requirements: Caller must delete[] the returned pointer when no longer needed.

functions.name: StrUtils::length
functions.description: Returns the length (in 16-bit code units) of a UTF-16-like string terminated by 0. Returns 0 for NULL or empty.
requirements: str must be a valid pointer to a 0-terminated uint16 sequence, or NULL.

functions.name: rotYXZ
functions.description: Builds a quaternion from Euler angles applied in Y, then X, then Z order by constructing a mat4 and extracting rotation.
requirements: Angles are in radians.

functions.name: boxNormal
functions.description: Returns one of the axis-aligned face normals (±X or ±Z) based on x and z modulo 1024, partitioning the square into four regions.

functions.name: Sphere::intersect
functions.description: Tests if two spheres intersect by comparing squared center distance with squared sum of radii.

functions.name: Box::intersection2D
functions.description: Computes 2D intersection rectangle in XY (z untouched) between this and b. Returns zero-size box if no overlap.

functions.name: Box::center
functions.description: Returns the center point of the box as (min+max)/2.

functions.name: Box::size
functions.description: Returns the size vector max-min.

functions.name: Box::expand
functions.description: Expands the box by subtracting v from min and adding v to max.

functions.name: Box::rotate90
functions.description: Rotates the box around Y axis in 90-degree increments n∈{0,1,2,3} by swapping and negating bounds.
requirements: n must be 0,1,2, or 3; asserts otherwise.

functions.name: Box::translate
functions.description: Translates the box by offset, adding to both min and max.

functions.name: Box::closestPoint
functions.description: Returns the point in the box closest to p by clamping each coordinate to [min,max].

functions.name: Box::contains
functions.description: Returns true if v lies inside the box inclusive of faces.

functions.name: Box::pushOut2D
functions.description: Computes the minimal 2D push-out vector along X or Z to move point v to the box boundary when v is inside.

functions.name: Box::intersect
functions.description: AABB-AABB intersection test in 3D.

functions.name: Color32::SetRGB15
functions.description: Sets this RGBA8888 color from a 16-bit RGB555 value; alpha set to 255.

functions.name: Color32::YCbCr_T871_420
functions.signature: static void Color32::YCbCr_T871_420(int32 Y0, int32 Y1, int32 Y2, int32 Y3, int32 Cb, int32 Cr, int32 F, Color32 &C0, Color32 &C1, Color32 &C2, Color32 &C3)
functions.description: Converts a 2x2 YCbCr 4:2:0 block (per ITU T.871) to four RGBA Color32 outputs with simple ordered dithering. F is 0 or 4 to select dither pattern row.
requirements: F must be 0 or 4 (asserts otherwise in debug).
Outputs C0..C3 are written in order.

functions.name: Stream::addPack
functions.description: Adds a ZIP pack file to the pack list if it exists in content. Loads central directory and prepares for file lookup.
requirements: name must refer to an accessible pack file under contentDir.
Up to MAX_PACKS packs can be added.
Returns false if not found or full.

functions.name: Stream::init
functions.description: Initializes streaming system by building the content file list via readFileList (platform-dependent).

functions.name: Stream::deinit
functions.description: Releases all loaded packs and clears file list.

functions.name: Stream::cacheRead
functions.signature: static void Stream::cacheRead(const char *name, Callback *callback = NULL, void *userData = NULL)
functions.description: Asynchronously/synchronously reads a cached file named 'name' into a Stream and passes it to callback. On Android, special-cases 'settings' to use osReadSlot.
requirements: name may be NULL only if callback handles NULL; generally must be valid.
callback may be NULL for synchronous platforms; behavior platform-dependent.
Relies on external osCacheRead/osReadSlot implementations.

functions.name: Stream::cacheWrite
functions.signature: static void Stream::cacheWrite(const char *name, const char *data, int size, Callback *callback = NULL, void *userData = NULL)
functions.description: Writes data of given size to cache under 'name', then invokes callback with a new Stream for that data. On Android, 'settings' uses osWriteSlot.
requirements: name must be non-NULL for meaningful operation.
data must point to at least size bytes.
Relies on external osCacheWrite/osWriteSlot implementations.

functions.name: Stream::fixBackslash
functions.description: On Xbox platforms, converts '/' to '\' in-place. No-ops on others.
requirements: str must be a writable null-terminated string.

functions.name: Stream::exists
functions.description: Checks file existence by attempting to open for read. On Linux, delegates to osFixFileName and checks for non-NULL return.
requirements: On Linux, osFixFileName must be provided; returns true if it returns non-NULL.
On other platforms, name must not be NULL.

functions.name: Stream::existsContent
functions.description: Checks for content existence by searching packs, then cached file list, then filesystem under contentDir.
requirements: name must be non-NULL.
Packs must have been added for pack search to succeed.

functions.name: Stream::setPos
functions.description: Sets the current logical read position in the stream.
requirements: pos should be within [0,size] for subsequent reads.

functions.name: Stream::seek
functions.description: Moves the current logical read position by offset bytes.
requirements: Resulting position should remain within [0,size] for subsequent reads.

functions.name: Stream::raw
functions.description: Reads count bytes into data from either file or memory buffer, with optional internal buffering for files. Advances position.
requirements: data must point to at least count writable bytes.
count>=0; if 0, function returns immediately.
For file mode with buffering, may allocate internal buffer; ensure stream opened successfully.

functions.name: Stream::read
functions.description: Reads sizeof(T) bytes into x from stream and returns x by reference.
requirements: Stream position must have at least sizeof(T) bytes remaining.
T must be trivially copyable for raw read semantics.

functions.name: Stream::readLE16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit little-endian value from the stream.
requirements: Stream must have at least 2 bytes available.

functions.name: Stream::readLE32

functions.name: BitStream::readBit
functions.description: Reads and returns the next bit (LSB-first) from the bitstream, refilling from the next byte when needed.
requirements: data pointer must be less than end when refilling; asserts otherwise in debug.

functions.name: BitStream::read
functions.description: Reads count bits LSB-first and returns them as an integer. Optimized for certain counts when byte-aligned.
requirements: count>=0.
Must not read past end; asserts may catch overflow in debug.

functions.name: BitStream::readBE
functions.description: Reads count bits MSB-first from the stream and returns them in the low bits of the result byte.
requirements: 1<=count<=8 recommended; function returns uint8.
Must not read past end; asserts in debug.

functions.name: BitStream::readBitBE
functions.description: Reads a single bit MSB-first from the stream.
requirements: Must not read past end; asserts in debug.

functions.name: BitStream::readByte
functions.description: Reads and returns the next byte from the underlying data.
requirements: data < end; asserts otherwise in debug.

functions.name: BitStream::readWord
functions.description: Reads the next 16-bit word from the stream with selected endianness and advances data by 2 bytes.
requirements: At least 2 bytes must remain in the stream data.

functions.name: BitStream::readU
functions.description: Reads count bits (up to any size) LSB-first, using a 16-bit buffer refill strategy. Returns the bits as an unsigned integer.
requirements: count>=0.
Underlying data must have enough bits; asserts may catch overflow.

functions.name: BitStream::skip
functions.description: Skips count bits by calling readU(count) and discarding result.
requirements: count>=0.
Sufficient bits must remain.

functions.name: FixedStr::get
functions.description: Copies the fixed-size array data into dst and appends a null terminator. Writes N bytes from data and then sets dst[N]=0.
requirements: dst must have space for at least N+1 bytes.
data must be initialized.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzers that consume raw bytes via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We craft byte sequences that are valid and interesting for the BitStream tests
# (which examine LSB-first and MSB-first bit ordering, endianness of 16-bit words),
# as well as for fnv32, qsort/sort (which derive ints from groups of 4 bytes).
# Strategy:
# - Produce lengths that cover boundary conditions required by the stubs:
#   * >=0 for fnv32 (allow empty)
#   * >=1 for BitStream::readBit/read/readBE/readBitBE/readByte
#   * >=2 for readWord/readU/skip
# - Include crafted patterns to exercise interesting bit layouts and endianness.
# - Stay within 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Predefined interesting 1-byte, 2-byte, and 4-byte patterns
ONE_BYTE_PATTERNS = [
    0x00,  # all zeros
    0xFF,  # all ones
    0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80,  # single bits
    0x7F, 0x80, 0x81,
    0x55, 0xAA,  # alternating
    0x3C, 0xC3,  # mirrored-ish
]

TWO_BYTE_PATTERNS = [
    (0x00, 0x00), (0xFF, 0xFF),
    (0x01, 0x00), (0x00, 0x01),  # endianness probe
    (0x34, 0x12), (0x12, 0x34),  # LE vs BE common
    (0x55, 0xAA), (0xAA, 0x55),
    (0x7F, 0x80), (0x80, 0x7F),
]

FOUR_BYTE_PATTERNS = [
    (0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),
    (0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # small positive int
    (0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # 255
    (0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00),
    (0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12),  # LE 0x12345678
    (0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78),  # BE 0x12345678 (when read as bytes for grouping)
    (0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # sign boundary
    (0x7F, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),  # INT_MAX bits pattern in LE bytes
    (0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80),  # INT_MIN bits pattern in LE bytes
    (0x55, 0xAA, 0x55, 0xAA),
]

# Build a palette of variable-length sequences that meet minimal size constraints used by stubs
SEQUENCES: List[bytes] = []

# Empty for fnv32/qsort/sort count=0 paths
SEQUENCES.append(b"")

# Length 1 sequences for BitStream single-byte tests
for b in ONE_BYTE_PATTERNS:
    SEQUENCES.append(bytes([b]))

# Length 2 sequences for readWord/readU/skip minimal
for a, b in TWO_BYTE_PATTERNS:
    SEQUENCES.append(bytes([a, b]))

# Length 4 sequences to feed multiple items for sort/qsort and cross 2-byte + next bytes for BitStream
for t in FOUR_BYTE_PATTERNS:
    SEQUENCES.append(bytes(t))

# Construct some longer mixed sequences that combine patterns and random tails
def mixed_sequence(rng: random.Random, total_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[int] = []
    # Start with a two-byte endian probe so BitStream readWord/readU have deterministic window
    a, b = rng.choice(TWO_BYTE_PATTERNS)
    parts.extend([a, b])
    # Add several 4-byte integers for sort/qsort
    n_groups = max(1, (total_len - 2) // 4)
    for _ in range(n_groups):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.extend(rng.choice(FOUR_BYTE_PATTERNS))
        else:
            # Random 4 bytes
            parts.extend([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)])
    # Trim or pad to desired length
    if len(parts) < total_len:
        parts.extend([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(total_len - len(parts))])
    return bytes(parts[:total_len])

# Deterministic seedable picker
def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a target class of sequence to generate
    mode = rng.randrange(0, 6)

    if mode == 0:
        # Return a predefined short sequence (covers empty/1/2/4)
        return rng.choice(SEQUENCES)

    if mode == 1:
        # Build a sequence ensuring >=1 byte length for BitStream single-bit tests
        base = rng.choice(ONE_BYTE_PATTERNS)
        # Optionally append a few random bytes
        extra_len = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        tail = bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(extra_len))
        return bytes([base]) + tail

    if mode == 2:
        # Ensure >=2 bytes for readWord/readU/skip, and align to multiple of 2
        a, b = rng.choice(TWO_BYTE_PATTERNS)
        buf = bytearray([a, b])
        # Add some alternating and random bytes
        pattern = [0x55, 0xAA]
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 8)):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                buf.append(pattern[len(buf) % 2])
            else:
                buf.append(rng.randrange(256))
        return bytes(buf)

    if mode == 3:
        # Compose several 4-byte patterns to populate qsort/sort items
        count = rng.randrange(1, 17)  # up to 16 items as in stubs
        buf = bytearray()
        for _ in range(count):
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                buf.extend(rng.choice(FOUR_BYTE_PATTERNS))
            else:
                # Random int with occasional extremes
                choice = rng.random()
                if choice < 0.2:
                    buf.extend((0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80))  # INT_MIN pattern (LE)
                elif choice < 0.4:
                    buf.extend((0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F))  # INT_MAX pattern (LE)
                else:
                    buf.extend([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)])
        return bytes(buf)

    if mode == 4:
        # Create a mixed sequence with target length between 8 and 256 bytes
        length = rng.randrange(8, 257)
        return mixed_sequence(rng, length)

    # mode == 5: longer but capped sequences to exercise BitStream across multiple bytes
    length = rng.randrange(257, min(1024, MAX_SIZE) + 1)
    return mixed_sequence(rng, length)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generate interesting ASCII text inputs to exercise StrUtils::toLower.
# The fuzzer copies up to 255 bytes and then appends a NUL terminator.

MAX_LEN = 255

UPPER = string.ascii_uppercase
LOWER = string.ascii_lowercase
DIGITS = string.digits
PUNCT = string.punctuation
WHITES = " \t\r\n\v\f"
MIXED_ASCII = LOWER + UPPER + DIGITS + PUNCT + WHITES

EDGE_NEAR_AZ = "@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{"

# Some non-ASCII bytes for robustness (Latin-1 range)
NON_ASCII_BYTES = bytes([0x7F, 0x80, 0x81, 0x9F, 0xA0, 0xC0, 0xDF, 0xE0, 0xF7, 0xFF])


def _rand_len(rng: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)


def _repeat_block(rng: random.Random, block: str, target_len: int) -> str:
    if not block or target_len <= 0:
        return ""
    reps = (target_len + len(block) - 1) // len(block)
    s = (block * reps)[:target_len]
    return s


def _alternating_case(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    flag = True
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha():
            out.append(ch.upper() if flag else ch.lower())
            flag = not flag
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)


def _insert_nuls(rng: random.Random, data: bytearray, prob: float = 0.2) -> None:
    if len(data) == 0:
        return
    if rng.random() < prob:
        idx = rng.randrange(0, len(data))
        data[idx] = 0


def _make_case_rich_string(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    segments = [EDGE_NEAR_AZ, UPPER, LOWER, DIGITS, PUNCT, WHITES]
    base = ''.join(segments)
    parts.append(_repeat_block(rng, base, min(max(length // 2, 0), len(base))))
    remaining = max(length - sum(len(p) for p in parts), 0)
    if remaining > 0:
        parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(MIXED_ASCII) for _ in range(remaining)))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    s_list = list(s)
    rng.shuffle(s_list)
    return ''.join(s_list)


def _scenario_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    scenarios: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty string
    scenarios.append(b"")

    # 2) Single characters around boundaries
    scenarios.append(b"A")
    scenarios.append(b"Z")
    scenarios.append(b"a")
    scenarios.append(b"z")
    scenarios.append(b"@")
    scenarios.append(b"[")
    scenarios.append(b"`")
    scenarios.append(b"{")

    # 3) All uppercase A-Z
    scenarios.append(UPPER.encode('ascii'))

    # 4) Mixed upper/lower alternating
    alt = _alternating_case("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
    scenarios.append(alt.encode('ascii'))

    # 5) Path-like with backslashes
    path = "C:\\Users\\TEST\\Documents\\FILE.TXT"
    scenarios.append(path.encode('ascii'))

    # 6) URL-like
    url = "HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/Path/To/Resource?Q=ABC&x=YZ"
    scenarios.append(url.encode('ascii'))

    # 7) Long string near max length with diverse chars
    long_len = 255
    long_s = _make_case_rich_string(rng, long_len)
    scenarios.append(long_s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore'))

    # 8) String with whitespace and punctuation
    ws = "\t \n\r ABC xyz 123 !? (Test) [CASE] {MiXeD}"
    scenarios.append(ws.encode('ascii'))

    # 9) Repeated block to fill length
    block = "AbCdEfG123_"
    rep = _repeat_block(rng, block, 200)
    scenarios.append(rep.encode('ascii'))

    # 10) Include some non-ASCII bytes and extended values
    na = bytearray()
    na.extend(b"AZaz ")
    na.extend(NON_ASCII_BYTES)
    pad = ''.join(rng.choice(MIXED_ASCII) for _ in range(30)).encode('ascii')
    na.extend(pad)
    _insert_nuls(rng, na, prob=0.5)
    scenarios.append(bytes(na))

    # 11) Lowercase already
    scenarios.append(LOWER.encode('ascii'))

    # 12) Digits and punctuation only
    dp = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS + PUNCT) for _ in range(60))
    scenarios.append(dp.encode('ascii'))

    return scenarios


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    scenarios = _scenario_strings(rng)

    # Randomly decide which scenario to emit, but bias towards long inputs
    weights = [
        1,  # empty
        1, 1, 1, 1,  # single char tests
        1, 1, 1, 1,  # boundary symbols (fixed bug: count matches scenarios)
        2,  # A-Z
        2,  # alternating
        2,  # path
        2,  # URL
        5,  # long mixed
        2,  # whitespace and punctuation
        3,  # repeated block
        3,  # non-ascii and NULs
        2,  # lowercase
        2,  # digits+punct
    ]

    # Ensure weights length matches scenarios length
    if len(weights) != len(scenarios):
        # Fallback: uniform selection if mismatch
        idx = rng.randrange(len(scenarios))
    else:
        idx = rng.choices(range(len(scenarios)), weights=weights, k=1)[0]

    data = bytearray(scenarios[idx])

    # Occasionally tweak: append a suffix or truncate to random length within bound
    if data:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            new_len = rng.randint(0, min(len(data), MAX_LEN))
            data = data[:new_len]
        if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(data) < MAX_LEN:
            tail_len = rng.randint(1, min(16, MAX_LEN - len(data)))
            tail = ''.join(rng.choice(MIXED_ASCII) for _ in range(tail_len)).encode('ascii')
            data.extend(tail)
            if len(data) > MAX_LEN:
                data = data[:MAX_LEN]

    if len(data) > MAX_LEN:
        data = data[:MAX_LEN]

    return bytes(data)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: C-string (null-terminated). The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to
# populate FixedStr<16> (str16) and StrUtils::copy. We should return an initial buffer
# that the harness may use to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. The buffer
# should therefore contain interesting, valid C-strings, including edge cases for
# FixedStr<16> such as lengths 0, <16, exactly 16, and >16, as well as varied byte
# content (ASCII, punctuation, whitespace, repeated chars), but always null-terminated.
# We pack multiple strings consecutively, each terminated by '\0'. The harness typically
# consumes a single std::string from FUZZ_PARAM_STR; supplying multiple options allows
# the fuzzer to slice, but to stay generic we craft a single composite where the first
# string is the most interesting for str16 behavior.
#
# Constraints:
# - Return bytes length <= 4096.
# - No external I/O. Deterministic given seed, but with variation.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_.,:/\\@#%+*=()[]{}<>|~^$"  # include slash and backslash for path-like cases
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"

CONTROL_BYTES = [
    0x07,  # bell
    0x08,  # backspace
    0x09,  # tab
    0x0A,  # newline
    0x0D,  # carriage return
]


def _rand_from_charset(rng: random.Random, n: int, charset: str) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))


def _make_exact_len(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # For exact length n (before NUL), prefer safe ascii; mix in punct/space occasionally
    parts: List[str] = []
    while len(''.join(parts)) < n:
        remain = n - len(''.join(parts))
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            chunk = _rand_from_charset(rng, min(remain, rng.randint(1, max(1, remain))), SAFE_ASCII)
        elif choice < 0.8:
            chunk = _rand_from_charset(rng, min(remain, rng.randint(1, max(1, remain))), SAFE_ASCII + PUNCT)
        else:
            # include whitespace runs
            wlen = min(remain, rng.randint(1, max(1, remain)))
            chunk = _rand_from_charset(rng, wlen, SAFE_ASCII + WHITESPACE)
        parts.append(chunk)
    s = ''.join(parts)
    return s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"


def _make_path_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a plausible file/path-like C-string
    roots = ["/", "./", "../", "C:/", "\\\\server\\share\\"]
    exts = [".txt", ".bin", ".cfg", ".zip", ".dat", ""]
    seps = ["/", "\\\\"]
    segs = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        seg = _rand_from_charset(rng, rng.randint(1, 8), SAFE_ASCII + "-_")
        segs.append(seg)
    fname = _rand_from_charset(rng, rng.randint(1, 10), SAFE_ASCII + "-_") + rng.choice(exts)
    prefix = rng.choice(roots)
    sep = rng.choice(seps)
    path = prefix + sep.join(segs + [fname]) if segs else prefix + fname
    return path.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"


def _make_repeated_char(rng: random.Random, length: int, ch: str) -> bytes:
    return (ch * length).encode('ascii') + b"\x00"


def _make_control_heavy(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    buf = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            buf.append(rng.choice(CONTROL_BYTES))
        else:
            buf.append(ord(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII + PUNCT + WHITESPACE)))
    # Ensure it doesn't contain embedded NUL; C-string termination is explicit at end
    for i, b in enumerate(buf):
        if b == 0:
            buf[i] = ord('A')
    buf.append(0)
    return bytes(buf)


def _dedup_and_trim(blobs: List[bytes], limit: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    seen = set()
    for b in blobs:
        if b in seen:
            continue
        if len(out) + len(b) > limit:
            break
        out += b
        seen.add(b)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # We craft a suite targeting FixedStr<16> boundary cases foremost:
    N = 16

    # 1) Empty string
    empty = b"\x00"

    # 2) Short string (<16)
    short_len = rng.randint(1, N - 1)
    short = _make_exact_len(rng, short_len)

    # 3) Exactly 16 bytes before NUL (to test no space for terminator in storage)
    exact16 = _make_exact_len(rng, N)

    # 4) Longer than 16 (to exercise truncation and zero padding in FixedStr)
    long_len = rng.randint(N + 1, N + 32)
    longer = _make_exact_len(rng, long_len)

    # 5) Path-like string to tickle StrUtils and potential path normalization
    pathlike = _make_path_like(rng)

    # 6) Repeated chars and whitespace-heavy
    reps = [
        _make_repeated_char(rng, N, 'A'),
        _make_repeated_char(rng, N + 5, '0'),
        (" " * (N - 1)).encode('ascii') + b"\x00",
    ]

    # 7) Control-heavy but still valid C-string (no embedded NULs)
    controly = _make_control_heavy(rng, rng.randint(4, N + 8))

    # 8) Mixed punctuation
    punct = (_rand_from_charset(rng, rng.randint(5, N + 5), SAFE_ASCII + PUNCT)).encode('ascii') + b"\x00"

    # Shuffle to vary first element sometimes, but bias to keep boundary cases early.
    blobs = [empty, short, exact16, longer, pathlike, punct, controly] + reps
    rng.shuffle(blobs)

    # Ensure we still include at least one of each key boundary at the front by re-inserting
    # deduped versions at the beginning in deterministic order.
    front = [empty, exact16, longer]
    # Build final sequence with size cap
    combined = _dedup_and_trim(front + blobs, 4096)
    return combined

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path (ASCII/UTF-8). Used by Stream::addPack to try to open a ZIP pack.
# The fuzzer stub preprends "nonexistent_dir/" to our provided string. We should return interesting path
# segments that exercise path normalization, separators, extensions, long names, relative components, and
# characters that may be treated specially on some platforms, while keeping it valid and under 4096 bytes.
# No files are actually accessed by this generator; it only returns bytes.

# Strategy
# - Generate a mix of path segments: normal names, dots, dot-dot, long segments, unicode-ish ASCII, mixed separators.
# - Provide various archive-like extensions (.zip, .pak, .ZIP) to try different code paths where code might check extensions.
# - Include cases with trailing slashes, leading slashes, drive-like prefixes (C:\\), and mixed separators.
# - Keep outputs valid UTF-8 and safe; avoid NULs.
# - Ensure determinism with seed, but still varied across calls with different seeds.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"

EXTS = [".zip", ".ZIP", ".Zip", ".pak", ".PCK", ".dat", ".bin", ""]

SPECIAL_SEGMENTS = [
    ".",
    "..",
    "...",
    "con", "prn", "nul", "aux",  # Windows device names
    "COM1", "LPT1",
    "pack", "data", "assets", "Textures", "Saves",
]

SEP_VARIANTS = ["/", "\\\\", "/\\\\", "//", "\\\\/", "/./", "/../"]

DRIVE_PREFIXES = ["", "C:", "D:", "Z:", "\\\\?\\\\", "\\\\.\\\\"]

# Some prebuilt interesting filenames
BASE_FILES = [
    "game.zip",
    "archive.ZIP",
    "level.pak",
    "textures.dat",
    "pack.bin",
    "中文.zip",  # keep ASCII only in bytes: fallback transliteration below
    "sp ace.zip",
    "mix-ed_Case.Zip",
    "longname_" + ("a" * 120) + ".zip",
]

# Encode to ASCII/UTF-8, replacing non-ASCII with ASCII approximations or hex escapes
def safe_encode(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        o = ord(ch)
        if 32 <= o < 127 and ch != "\x00":
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            # replace with hex-like escape to keep ASCII and avoid NULs
            out.append("_%02X" % (o & 0xFF))
    return "".join(out)

def rand_segment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return rng.choice(SPECIAL_SEGMENTS)
    elif choice < 0.55:
        # random safe ascii segment
        length = rng.randint(1, 32)
        return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII + " .@$") for _ in range(length)).strip()
    elif choice < 0.8:
        # numeric segment
        return str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))
    else:
        # long segment
        length = rng.randint(33, 128)
        return "seg_" + "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(length))

def build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # optionally include drive prefix or UNC-like
    prefix = rng.choice(DRIVE_PREFIXES)
    # number of segments (excluding filename)
    seg_count = rng.randint(0, 6)
    segs: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(seg_count):
        segs.append(rand_segment(rng))
        # occasionally inject special separators like ./ or ../
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            segs.append(rng.choice([".", ".."]))

    # filename base
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base = rng.choice(BASE_FILES)
    else:
        base = rand_segment(rng)
        # ensure a plausible extension in many cases to hint at pack-like files
        if rng.random() < 0.85:
            base += rng.choice(EXTS)

    # mix in separator variants
    sep = rng.choice(SEP_VARIANTS)
    # Construct path, carefully handling empty segments
    parts = [s for s in segs if s != ""]
    path = prefix
    if prefix and not prefix.endswith(":") and not prefix.endswith("\\\\"):
        # ensure a separator after special prefixes unless we will add our own
        path += sep
    elif prefix and (prefix.endswith(":")):
        # drive like C: may or may not have separator
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            path += sep
    if parts:
        path += sep.join(parts)
        if not path.endswith(SEP_VARIANTS[0]) and rng.random() < 0.3:
            path += sep
    # append base
    if path and not path.endswith(sep):
        if not path.endswith("/") and not path.endswith("\\"):
            path += rng.choice(["/", "\\\\", sep])
    path += base

    # optional trailing separator (less common)
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        path += rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"])

    # sanitize to ASCII-safe string
    path = safe_encode(path)

    # limit total size; the fuzzer will prepend "nonexistent_dir/", so keep margin
    max_len = 3800
    if len(path) > max_len:
        # keep filename tail
        tail = path[-256:]
        path = path[: max_len - len(tail) - 1] + "/" + tail

    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose among several path archetypes
    archetype = rng.randint(0, 7)

    if archetype == 0:
        # Simple filename with extension
        name = "pack_" + "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12))) + rng.choice(EXTS)
    elif archetype == 1:
        # Nested relative path with dot/dotdot
        parts = [rng.choice([".", "..", "assets", "data", "packs"]) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))]
        parts += ["archive" + rng.choice(EXTS)]
        name = "/".join(parts)
    elif archetype == 2:
        # Windows-like path
        drive = rng.choice(["C:", "D:", "E:"])
        parts = ["Users", "fuzz", "AppData", "Local", "Game"]
        # mutate a few parts
        for i in range(len(parts)):
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                parts[i] = parts[i].lower()
        name = drive + "\\\\" + "\\\\".join(parts) + "\\\\" + "data" + rng.choice(EXTS)
    elif archetype == 3:
        # UNC-like with mixed separators
        name = "\\\\?\\\\C:" + rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"]) + "path" + rng.choice(["/", "\\\\"]) + "archive" + rng.choice(EXTS)
    elif archetype == 4:
        # Long, many segments
        segs = [rand_segment(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12))]
        name = "/".join(segs) + "/" + rand_segment(rng) + rng.choice(EXTS)
    elif archetype == 5:
        # Include spaces and special names
        segs = [rng.choice(["Program Files", "My Documents", "aux", "con"]) for _ in range(3)]
        name = "/".join(segs) + "/game.zip"
    elif archetype == 6:
        # Direct base file from list
        name = rng.choice(BASE_FILES)
    else:
        # Fully randomized via builder
        name = build_path(rng)

    name = safe_encode(name)

    # Final safety and length cap
    if len(name) > 4000:
        name = name[:4000]

    return name.encode("utf-8")
